whatWeChecked: The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.
The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.

pros: Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
No independent audit of the models.
redFlags: Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.
A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.
Performance language with no dates attached.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
We rate it 4.5 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$250 minimum is the right size for testing either.
